text.p: The following are the main stories from Wednesday morning's German newspapers:
FRANKFURTER ALLGEMEINE ZEITUNG
- Klaus Zwickel, leader of the IG Metall trade union, says crisis in steel industry not over.
- Labour Minister Norbert Bluem rejects stance of Free Democrat (FDP) coalition partners on pensions policy.
- Foerign Minister Klaus Kinkel delays departure to Ankara to check authenticity of controversial comments about him atttributed to Turkish prime minister.
- German Federation of Employers' Associations (BDA) wants reforms of social security and labour costs to proceed more quickly.
- Government tax plans will lead to an explosion in government debt, opposition Social Democrats (SPD) say.
HANDELSBLATT
- Steelworkers demonstrate in Frankfurt against power on German banks.
- Plant construction jobs increasingly being transferred abroad.
- Federal Cartel Office declares resistance to construction firm Hochtief's indirect control of rival Holzmann.
- Currency rate changes had positive effect on 1996 performance of carmaker BMW, company says.
SUEDDEUTSCHE ZEITUNG
- States of Bavaria and Berlin repatriate 41 Bosnian refugees.
- Bavarian economics minister Otto Wiesheu defends plans to give media group Kirch a big credit line.
- Rise in West German consumer prices slows in March.
- Eastern Germans working longer hours than western Germans, research from trade union institute shows.
DIE WELT
- Government and industry speak out in favour of beginning European monetary union (EMU) on time.
- Chancellor Helmut Kohl's coalition partners pressure him to declare soon whether he will run for re-election next year.
- Institute of German Economy (IW) says Germany can only meet EMU criteria with difficulty.
